# `uring` standard library

The `uring` module provides low-level Linux `io_uring` kernel submission and completion rings
for zero-copy, non-blocking asynchronous system calls.

```dva
#use uring
```

## Platform requirements

The `uring` module depends directly on the Linux kernel `io_uring` interface (kernel 5.1+).
It is available exclusively on Linux targets.

## Core structures

```dva
#type CQE (
   user_data: Int,
   res:       Int,
   flags:     Int
)

#type Ring (
   ring_fd:  Int,
   sqes:     Addr,
   sq_head:  Addr,
   sq_tail:  Addr,
   sq_mask:  Int,
   sq_array: Addr,
   cqes:     Addr,
   cq_head:  Addr,
   cq_tail:  Addr,
   cq_mask:  Int,
   sq_len:   Int,
   cq_len:   Int
)
```

## Function catalog

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uring::init` | `Int => < Ring | Error >` | Initializes an `io_uring` ring with specified submission queue entries |
| `uring::prep_read` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => ()` | Prepares an asynchronous read operation |
| `uring::prep_write` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => ()` | Prepares an asynchronous write operation |
| `uring::prep_nop` | `Ring, Int => ()` | Prepares a no-operation submission |
| `uring::submit` | `Ring => Int` | Enters kernel and submits pending SQEs |
| `uring::submit_and_wait` | `Ring, Int => Int` | Submits pending SQEs and blocks until at least `wait_nr` CQEs complete |
| `uring::peek_cqe` | `Ring => < CQE | >` | Checks if a completion queue entry is ready without blocking |
| `uring::cqe_seen` | `Ring => ()` | Advances completion queue head pointer |
| `uring::close` | `Ring => ()` | Unmaps submission/completion buffers and closes ring descriptor |
